name: Occipital Encephalocele

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Encephalocele

criteria.description: Presence of a midline occipital skull defect with herniation of intracranial contents
Neuroimaging (MRI or CT) demonstrating encephalocele sac containing brain tissue, meninges, and/or cerebrospinal fluid
Visible occipital mass or swelling present at birth
Presence of neurological impairments such as developmental delay or seizures

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a midline occipital skull defect with herniation of intracranial contents confirmed by neuroimaging and visible occipital mass at birth
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging studies; genetic testing may be considered for syndromic cases.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Occipital cranial defect with herniated brain tissue
pathognomonic.notes: Visible sac protruding from occipital region
searchTerms: back of head skull defect with brain herniation
occipital bone gap with brain tissue outside
brain tissue pushing through skull at back of head

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital occipital mass covered by skin or membrane
searchTerms: birthmark or lump on back of head covered by skin
congenital bump on back of head

common.notes: Variable severity depending on brain involvement
Often develops secondary to CSF flow obstruction
May present in infancy or early childhood

common.symptomName: Motor deficits including spasticity or paresis
common.notes: Depends on extent of brain tissue involvement

occasional.notes: May result from associated brain abnormalities
May be secondary to neurological impairment

rare.notes: Due to brainstem involvement or associated anomalies
Rarely observed depending on lesion extent
searchTerms: cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: Routine labs typically normal; CSF analysis if hydrocephalus or infection suspected
imaging: MRI brain showing occipital skull defect with herniation of meninges and brain tissue
CT scan demonstrating bony defect and encephalocele sac
Ultrasound in neonates for initial assessment
other: Prenatal ultrasound may detect encephalocele in utero
Elevated maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Herniation of meninges only without brain tissue
Lymphatic malformation without bony skull defect
Soft, compressible mass without intracranial communication

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of occipital mass
Signs of increased intracranial pressure (vomiting, lethargy)
references: NIH Genetic and Rare Diseases Information Center (GARD)
Surgical Management of Encephaloceles: A Review, Journal of Neurosurgery Pediatrics, 2020
